question: Why is the incident backlog finally dropping?

intro.title: Meet Marcus Webb
intro.text: IT Operations, Singapore. 3,120 endpoints, five sites, one workspace that already knows what today demands.

hero.title: The morning brief lands
hero.text: Backlog down to 47 incidents — 27 off the July peak. One catch: 214 endpoints still exposed to CVE-2026-31842 before Tuesday.

kpis.title: Four numbers, zero digging
kpis.text: Uptime 99.96%. Patch compliance 96.8%, up 2.1 points. MTTR down to 3.4 hours. Live from ServiceNow and Jira — no spreadsheet safari.

chart.title: The backlog story, drawn
chart.text: July spiked to 521 tickets on the gateway failover. August flipped it: 474 resolved against 447 opened. The queue is finally shrinking.

ask.title: Drag the number, ask why
ask.text: Marcus drops the incident card into chat and asks the question every boss asks: why is the backlog finally dropping?

delegate.title: One click, PO chased
delegate.text: Chase the Dell PO: Ariba checked, two approvers nudged, ship-split confirmed. $142,800 released four days before the quote expires.

autopilot.title: Approvals on autopilot
autopilot.text: Flip the switch. Low-risk expenses and routine access grants clear themselves — Marcus keeps the $142K PO and prod-access calls.

mcp.title: Plugged into everything
mcp.text: ServiceNow, Jira, Slack, GitHub — eight live connections. Every answer traced back to real systems, not vibes.

recap.title: Friday report, instantly
recap.text: One click compiles the week — backlog burned, 12 Austin access packs shipped early, CVE stragglers patched. Priya's update writes itself.

outro.title: Ops at machine speed
outro.text: Same Marcus. Same five fires. Now the busywork runs itself — and he runs the strategy.
